source: Massoudi and Fuge (2025) Agentic LLMs for conceptual systems engineering and design (cause of low requirement coverage)
finding: A manual audit found two causes of low requirement coverage: nodes left out the linked_reqs field, and requirement IDs drifted from the canonical format.
numbers: Coverage peaked at 20% (DeepSeek R1 70B, 9-role MAS, T=0.0). Drift examples: SR01 and SR-001 instead of SR-01. The exact-match evaluator counted these as misses. 5 seeds x 3 temperatures x 2 models x 2 configurations.
limits: So part of the loss is under-linking plus a strict string matcher, not proof that content was lost. True semantic coverage was not measured. Open-weight 70B models only.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 mostly answered: add a code-side requirements ledger with fixed IDs and a check that every node lists its IDs. No paper tested this fix, so the fix itself is untested.
quote: neither agent hierarchy nor reasoning fine-tuning alone suffices to encode system requirements

source: Massoudi and Fuge (2025) Agentic LLMs for conceptual systems engineering and design (ablation MAS vs two-agent)
finding: In the ablation, with the reasoning model the full staged system beat the two-agent loop on requirements coverage and graph size; the two-agent loop won on executability, completion and runtime.
numbers: MAS about 6 nodes and about 650 s; 2AS 1 node and under 40 s. Non-reasoning Llama 3.3 70B MAS often crashed (over 60,000 tokens or recursion limit), so its speed advantage over 2AS is an artefact.
limits: Time and token budgets are not equal between arms. The 2AS gain in executability partly comes from the one-node collapse.
agent_relevance: Staging buys coverage and detail but costs tokens and completion. Judge staged arms at equal tokens and report both sides.

source: Sprague et al. (2025) To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning (ICLR 2025)
finding: A meta-analysis of the CoT literature plus own tests on 20 datasets and 14 models found that CoT gains sit almost only in math and symbolic or logic tasks.
numbers: Mean CoT gain over direct answer: symbolic 14.2, math 12.3, logical 6.9 points. Top-three categories 56.9 with CoT vs 45.5 without. All other categories 56.8 vs 56.1. On MMLU and MMLU-Pro up to 95% of the CoT gain came from questions with an equals sign.
limits: CoT is a weak form of staging (free-form steps), not a Pahl-and-Beitz sequence. Open-ended design tasks were not in the set.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 (task type): expect staging to pay on formal or verifiable sub-steps (S2 evaluation, constraint checks) and little on open-ended idea generation. Route by task type.
quote: CoT can be applied selectively, maintaining performance while saving inference costs.

source: Meincke, Mollick, Mollick and Shapiro (2025) Prompting Science Report 2: the decreasing value of chain of thought in prompting
finding: On GPQA Diamond (198 questions, 25 trials each), CoT helped non-reasoning models a little and reasoning models almost not at all, while costing more time.
numbers: Non-reasoning models: Sonnet 3.5 large gain at the 100%-correct metric, but Gemini Flash 2.0 (RD -0.131, p<.001) and Gemini Pro 1.5 (RD -0.172, p<.001) lost on it; CoT took 35-600% more time. Reasoning models (o3-mini, o4-mini, Flash 2.5): small or no gains, o4-mini +0.056 at the 51% metric, Flash 2.5 -0.131 at 100%; 20-80% more time. Total trials N=4950 per condition.
limits: One benchmark (multiple-choice science). Prompt is a generic think-step-by-step, not a design process.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: the benefit of added structure shrinks or turns negative with stronger and reasoning models. Test the scaffold on a weak and a strong arm and keep a plain control for each.
quote: for dedicated reasoning models, the added benefits of explicit CoT prompting appear negligible

source: Goh, Kos and Goel (2026) Knowledge Model Prompting (TMK) increases LLM performance on planning tasks
finding: A structured task-method-knowledge prompt raised PlanBench Blocksworld accuracy for nearly every model, and most for the strongest reasoning model.
numbers: o1 Random: 31.5% to 97.33%; o1 Mystery 74.3% to 83.3%; o1 Classic 95.7% to 98.5%. GPT-4o Classic 35.5% to 45.3%; GPT-4 Classic 34.6% to 39.7%. o1-mini Random 9.33% to 27.0% but Mystery 19.1% to 16.83%.
limits: Token cost of the TMK prompt vs plain not equalised. Domain is formal planning. Mechanism claimed (steering to code-execution mode) is a hypothesis.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 counter-evidence: structure does not only help weak models; a rich scaffold can lift a strong reasoning model when the task is formal. The weak small model (o1-mini) got mixed results, so weak-benefits-more is not a rule.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) SELF-DISCOVER: LLMs self-compose reasoning structures
finding: Letting the model pick, adapt and implement its own reasoning structure from atomic modules beat fixed CoT and plan-and-solve, with one call per instance.
numbers: BBH/T4D/MATH: GPT-4 direct 58/51/70.5, CoT 75/52/71, Plan-and-Solve 73/53/70, Self-Discover 81/85/73. PaLM 2-L 56/30/45 direct, 67/69/50.5 Self-Discover. Uses 10-40x fewer inference calls than self-consistency or per-module methods.
limits: Structure is chosen once per task, not per step. Compared with fixed CoT, not with a fixed human design sequence. Authors are the method proposers.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 partial: model-chosen structure beats a fixed generic one on reasoning tasks. Supports letting the agent select which states and operators to run, but order flexibility inside one item was not tested.

source: Meincke et al. (2025): cost and variability of added reasoning steps
finding: Added reasoning steps cost real time and tokens, and for some models they also raise answer variability and lose items the model got right directly.
numbers: CoT requests took 35-600% more time for non-reasoning models and 20-80% (10-20 s) more for reasoning models; strict 25/25 reliability dropped for Gemini Flash 2.0, Gemini Pro 1.5 and GPT-4o-mini under the 90% or 100% metrics.
limits: Time stands in for tokens; exact token counts are in the paper tables, not extracted here.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: stage cost is real. Budget rule: a stage runs only if the task is formal or verifiable, and each stage is compared with a plain arm at equal tokens.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Understanding design fixation in generative AI
finding: A small user study found ChatGPT (GPT-4o) outputs for chair design repeat common themes and are less diverse than human Red Dot award entries.
numbers: Share of unique terms: human 78.2% vs ChatGPT 67.4%. 10 novice participants, chair design, observation plus interviews.
limits: N=10, one product category, GPT-4o only, qualitative coding; not a test of a persistence rule.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 (partly): fixation in the LLM itself is confirmed on a newer model, but no replication of Egea's concept-abandonment finding exists here. Use a forced-alternatives step (O1) and measure distinct concepts.

source: Jackson, Cha, Prikladnicki and van der Hoek (2026) The role of LLMs in collaborative software design
finding: In a lab study, professionals who used an LLM to design a bicycle-parking app sometimes anchored on the LLM's first appealing design and explored less.
numbers: 18 pairs of software professionals; shared-instance use helped shared understanding; parallel separate instances sometimes led to context drift.
limits: Exploratory, qualitative, software not hardware, no control group without LLM.
agent_relevance: Early convergence is a documented risk; supports a step that forces alternatives before committing in S2.

source: Search note (this run): LLM fixation replication and persistence rule
finding: Searches did not find a replication of Egea et al. (concept abandonment, fixation) on a frontier model, nor any test of a persistence rule.
numbers: One web search on LLM design fixation; hits were Egea (2024/2025 journal version), Chen (2025) and Jackson (2026). Search APIs (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, arXiv) were rate-limited this run, so the search is not exhaustive.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 stays open for the persistence rule.

source: Search note (this run): staged Pahl-and-Beitz prompt vs plain prompt at equal tokens
finding: No study found that runs a clarify-abstract-function-principle-evaluate prompt against a plain prompt on a frontier LLM at equal tokens, and none that ablates stage order vs stage content.
numbers: Two web searches plus reading Massoudi and Fuge, Self-Discover, TMK; none contains this comparison. API searches were blocked by rate limits.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1 and 2 stay open; the experiment is ours to run (arms: plain, generic extra steps, staged in order, staged shuffled).

source: Search note (this run): original German studies (Fricke, Ehrlenspiel and Dylla, Bender)
finding: The originals were not reachable open-access this run; the numbers still come second-hand through Motte (2015).
numbers: Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex returned HTTP 429; web search budget used up.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open; keep K02 and K03 labelled as relayed.

source: Search note (this run): early-structure sketches in LLM clarify and function stages
finding: No LLM study found that lets solution sketches appear inside requirement or function stages.
numbers: No hits; Jackson (2026) shows early LLM designs anchor people, which is indirect evidence of risk.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 stays open; test as an ablation: allow a draft solution in S1 but tag it as a hypothesis.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) SR-LLM: rethinking structured representation in LLMs
finding: Adding structured representations (AMR, logic forms) to prompts helped Llama3.1-8B consistently, GPT-3.5 mostly, and GPT-4o-mini only about half the time and by less.
numbers: Training-free, 3 models ordered weak to strong, CoT and one-shot, averaged over AMR, FOL and PST. Gains shrink as model strength rises.
limits: Structured representation is not a design process; absolute numbers not extracted here.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: second source that gain from added structure falls as the model gets stronger (agrees with Meincke; disagrees with Goh on o1).
quote: for stronger models, the additional structured information offers limited advantages

source: Massoudi and Fuge (2025): reasoning vs non-reasoning model inside staged pipeline
finding: Inside the same nine-role pipeline, the reasoning-distilled model finished runs and the non-reasoning model did not.
numbers: Only DeepSeek R1 70B flagged runs complete (M5>0); Llama 3.3 70B MAS often crashed. R1 MAS up to 6 +/- 1.9 nodes and 49 +/- 28% compilability.
limits: Different model families trained differently; 30 runs per cell group.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: a staged scaffold needs a model strong enough to hold the state; weak models break the pipeline instead of gaining from it.

source: Massoudi and Fuge (2025): requirement traceability design
finding: The design-state graph already carries a linked_reqs field per node, yet agents left it empty or mis-formatted; the authors advise strict regex parsing.
numbers: Coverage maximum 20%; embodiment tagging 100%; JSON validity 100%.
limits: No ablation with a programmatic tracker was run.
agent_relevance: A code-based ledger (fixed ID list, auto-check of unmet IDs after each stage) is the obvious untested fix for gap 3.
quote: rigorous regex-based parsing is essential to avoid both missed matches and false positives
